A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BDPO research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison despite expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic sampling experiments, D4RL policy evaluations, ablations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthetic and D4RL results, expanded ablations, and additional inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The pathwise KL objective, two-scale actor-critic updates, and LCB ensembles remain unchanged. V2 Table 3 reports a limited inference adaptation for antmaze-umaze-diverse-v0: executing one sampled action instead of selecting the highest-Q action from ten. The surrounding general ten-action description remains inconsistent with this exception.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six synthetic datasets, nine locomotion tasks, and six antmaze tasks. Moons already appears in v1's appendix; its inclusion in v2's main figures does not expand coverage. Added analyses use these existing tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds SRPO and EDP while retaining the existing comparators. V2 also introduces DAC into the synthetic generation comparison and adds an inference comparison against DAC, DTQL, QGPO, and JAX/PyTorch implementations of Diffusion-QL, substantially expanding comparative evidence.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the locomotion diffusion backbone from four 512-unit layers to four 256-unit layers and revises regularization settings across the benchmark, including halfcheetah eta from 0.5 to 0.05. Antmaze LCB coefficients and action sampling also change. New protocols include diffusion-step ablations and latency measurement over 10,000 states with batch size one.

E4.justification: Policy-parameterization ablations expand from two tasks to all nine locomotion tasks, and eta/rho sensitivity analyses expand from two tasks to four. V2 adds an N=2,5,10 diffusion-step ablation and DAC generation-path case studies testing the guidance mechanism.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed means and standard deviations, with ten locomotion or 100 antmaze evaluation episodes per seed. Added ablations retain this practice; no confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced. The latency experiment's 10,000 states constitute a new sample-size specification.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises BDPO results throughout: locomotion and antmaze totals change from 852.1 and 502.0 to 856.7 and 519.6 under revised configurations, not identical settings. Existing baseline entries also change, including DTQL antmaze-l-div from 66.4 to 54.0. New latency, DAC sampling, and ablation findings substantially extend the results.

T1.justification: Appendix C substantially revises the supporting mathematics. Theorem C.1 gains explicit optimization derivations; C.2 replaces the erroneous positive KL penalty with a negative penalty in its Bellman argument; C.4 separately develops environment-level and diffusion-step improvement. C.3 and C.5 gain local arguments where v1 largely referred to prior proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: pathwise KL regularization, equivalence of optimal policies, efficient two-scale actor-critic optimization, and strong synthetic/D4RL performance. Additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 specifically explains DAC's sampling mismatch through Q-value rather than diffusion-value guidance, interprets latency differences through backends and generation procedures, and motivates five diffusion steps as an efficiency/performance tradeoff. The earlier core interpretations and applicability scope remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link advertised as providing code and results, explicitly lists behavior-policy learning rates, and documents inference backends and timing procedures. Hyperparameter tables are revised, while most architecture, optimizer, training-budget, and hardware information already existed in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Jia et al. on policy rehearsing, Shribak et al. on diffusion spectral representations, and Song et al. on DDIM. It modestly broadens related-work coverage and sharpens the comparison with DAC without changing BDPO's principal research positioning.

P1.justification: The overall section structure and much of the prose remain. V2 edits the abstract and terminology, expands explanations, reorders Section 5.3's analyses, brings runtime discussion into the main text, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement.

P2.justification: V2 widens Table 1 with additional comparator columns, adds a runtime table, and extensively revises experimental displays. Synthetic-path figures gain intermediate panels, the combined sensitivity figure becomes two expanded figures, and new latency, DAC-generation, full parameterization, and diffusion-step plots are added.

improvement.justification: Expanded proof arguments, the corrected KL-penalty sign, broader ablations, and direct DAC comparisons improve the paper's support and auditability. Added access and timing details also help. These gains are tempered by inconsistent one-versus-ten-action descriptions and the new claim of about 10% latency overhead despite Figure 12 showing approximately 20–24%. Higher benchmark totals under changed configurations do not themselves establish improvement.
